verdict.reason: Verified independently in the working tree. `assertPlainTabId`/`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` exist only in `worksheet-images.controller.ts` (declared at :51-55, applied at :82 inside `worksheetOrThrow` and at :95 in `getImages`); a repo-wide grep for `assertPlainTabId|UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` returns no other production file. The sibling tab-scoped controllers carry a byte-identical, unguarded `worksheetOrThrow` that keys `root.sheets?.[tabId]` with the raw URL param and then writes to the result: worksheet-styles.controller.ts:50-57 → :94 (`.rangeStyles = rangeStyles`) and :134-138 (`sheetStyle`); worksheet-charts.controller.ts:45-52 → :106-110 (`ws.charts = {}`); worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:43-47 → :90 and :136; worksheet-rules.controller.ts:55-59 → :99 and :142; worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:53-57 → :136/:181/:226/:271; cells.controller.ts:158 and :193. All of these declare the same route prefix `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId` with the same guards (e.g. worksheet-styles.controller.ts:33-34 vs worksheet-images.controller.ts:57-58), so the same request shape the new images guard refuses still reaches them. I looked for a shared upstream sanitizer and found none: no global pipe/middleware in `main.ts:65` area or `workspace-scope.guard.ts` filters `tabId`, and the only other defence in the repo is the membership check in worksheet-structure.controller.ts:104-113 using `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33), which the six siblings do not use. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane — a new guard with reachable bypasses in code the diff does not show — and the impact (write landing on `Object.prototype` / prototype-key confusion on a reachable authenticated route) is critical.

Also :237 and :730 read `root.sheets?.[tabId]` from `tabOrder`, which is safe, but the body-supplied path at :315 is not. verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (comments.controller.ts:315 body-supplied tabId, :323-326 truthiness tab check, :330-332 `ws.comments = {}` write, and no import of the new `assertPlainTabId`/`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` from worksheet-images.controller.ts:51-55). However the claimed harm — the write landing on `Object.prototype` — is unreachable. Between the truthiness check and the mutation, line :327 calls `sheetCellAnchor`, which at :653-660 demands `worksheet.rowOrder?.[r-1]` and `worksheet.colOrder?.[c-1]` be truthy and otherwise throws BadRequestException; this runs BEFORE `doc.update` at :329. Any object reached via a prototype-shaped key (`Object.prototype` for `__proto__`, `Object` for `constructor`, a function for `toString`) has neither property, so the request 400s and `ws.comments = {}` never executes. On the production path it fails even earlier: yorkie.service.ts:36-57 always attaches a real yorkie.Document, and worksheet-structure.controller.ts:88-90 documents that the object proxy's get trap reads a real Map and answers `undefined` for `__proto__`, so :326 throws 404. Reaching the write would first require Object.prototype.rowOrder AND .colOrder to already be populated arrays by some other route — a separate finding at that route, not a reachable bypass here. Refuted on already-guarded; the residual observation (a 400 instead of a 404 on a plain-object fixture) is cosmetic, not blocking.

mergedFrom.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with the generic `detachYorkieValue`, but a docs-range anchor's `posRange` is explicitly documented as a value that does not survive a generic detach. `GET /comments` on a `doc` document therefore returns a `posRange` made of Yorkie CRDT metadata instead of a usable `TreePosStructRange`, so an API consumer cannot resolve or round-trip a docs thread anchor.

finding.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with `detachYorkieValue`, which this repo documents as broken for Yorkie *array* proxies — and two of the three live anchor shapes carry arrays (`pdf-text.rects`, `docs-range.posRange`). Every `GET /comments`, `PATCH :threadId` and `POST :threadId/replies` response for a PDF or docs document created in the editor will therefore return CRDT metadata in place of those arrays.
finding.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:13-20` states outright that `detachYorkieValue` "branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata" — and `comment-ops.ts`'s own `isThread` docblock repeats the same fact. The anchors that reach `copyThread` do contain arrays: `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:61` stores `rects: Array.from(anchor.rects ?? []).map(copyRect)` for a `pdf-text` anchor (and deliberately uses `Array.from` rather than a spread "because a spread would carry live proxy objects out of the CRDT"); `packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31` types a docs anchor's `posRange` as `TreePosStructRange`, a two-element tuple. `comments.controller.ts` returns `copyThread` output straight to the client for every doc/pdf thread it did not itself create. The comment-ops docblock even cites `pdf-comment-store.ts`'s field-by-field `copyAnchor` as the bug being avoided, while choosing the one helper that reintroduces it for arrays.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `copyThread` does not detach the anchor with `detachYorkieValue`: at packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts:128 it calls `detachAnchor`, which at :106-109 first routes any value exposing `toJSON` (i.e. every live Yorkie proxy, the only case where the `Array.isArray` trap applies) through `unwrapJson` — the proxy's own snapshot path that serializes nested arrays correctly. `detachYorkieValue` at :116 is only a fallback for a value with no `toJSON` (a plain object, whose arrays satisfy `Array.isArray` and are handled correctly at yorkie-json.ts:172-174) or when the repaired parse throws. The file's own docblock at :93-102 states this ("Not `detachYorkieValue` alone … The proxy's own `toJSON` … is tried first"), and comment-ops.spec.ts:284-324 is a regression test for exactly the named `docs-range.posRange` array case, asserting the copy returns `[{offset:3},{offset:9}]` rather than `{createdAt, movedAt}`. The claimed consequence — every GET/PATCH/replies response for a PDF or docs thread returning CRDT metadata (comments.controller.ts:304, :334, :599) — therefore does not hold on the live-proxy path. The reviewer quoted yorkie-json.ts:13-20 correctly as a description of `detachYorkieValue` standalone but misread the call site, which already applies the guard that docblock prescribes.

finding.summary: `duplicateTab` copies the worksheet verbatim, so the copy's charts (and its `pivotTable`) still carry `sourceTabId` pointing at the ORIGINAL tab. `chart-utils.ts` resolves chart data with `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`, so every chart on the duplicated tab renders the source tab's numbers, not the copy's — and a duplicated pivot output tab silently becomes a second dependent that makes the new `resolveDelete` refuse to delete the source tab, naming a tab the user never configured.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/chart-utils.ts:116 `const sourceSheet = root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId];` (same at :188 and :281), and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/pivot/use-pivot-table.ts:135 `const sourceWs = root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId];`. The new duplicate writes `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts, duplicateTab) — chart ids and `sourceTabId`/`pivotTable.sourceTabId` are not remapped to the new tab id. Fix belongs in `duplicateTab`.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `duplicateTab` copies the worksheet verbatim, leaving chart `sourceTabId` and `pivotTable.sourceTabId` pointing at the original tab. The actual implementation does the opposite. At packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:184-192 it rebuilds the `charts` map and rewrites `sourceTabId` to `newTabId` for every chart that was self-sourced (`chart.sourceTabId === tabId`), leaving foreign-sourced charts intentionally untouched; at tab-ops.ts:193 it `delete copy.pivotTable`, and at tab-ops.ts:178 it omits `kind: 'pivot'` from the copied `TabMeta`. Consequently the chart-utils.ts lookups the finding cites (`root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]` at chart-utils.ts:116, :188, :281) resolve to the duplicate's own worksheet, not the source tab's, so no chart renders the wrong numbers. And because the copy carries no `pivotTable`, `resolveDelete`'s dependent scan (tab-ops.ts:85-89, which reads `root.sheets[id].pivotTable.sourceTabId`) cannot pick it up, so the "second dependent blocks deleting the source tab" consequence cannot occur; use-pivot-table.ts never sees a definition on the copy either. Existing tests pin both behaviours: tab-ops.spec.ts:214-232 asserts the self-sourced chart is repointed to `copy.id` while the foreign one stays at `other.id`, and tab-ops.spec.ts:234-249 asserts `pivotTable` and `kind` are dropped and that `resolveDelete(root,'tab-1')` names only the original output tab. The remaining sub-claim that chart ids are not remapped is not a defect: chart maps are per-worksheet and every consumer indexes them tab-scoped (chart-object-layer.tsx:58, sheet-view.tsx:247/444/480, worksheet-charts.controller.ts:110), so identical chart ids across two sheets never collide. Ground: not-present — the code is not as described.
